title: Strictly semistable local uniformization along centred valuations
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $X$ be a $T$-curve with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There are finitely many integral strictly semistable $T$-curves $Y_i$ [def-trf-strictly-semistable-curve] and birational quasi-modifications $Y_i\to X$ such that every centred valuation of every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$ lifts to some $Y_i$. Each generic map $(Y_i)_\eta\to X_\eta$ induced by $Y_i\to X$ identifies $(Y_i)_\eta$ with an open subscheme. A $T$-curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]) $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one, without a separatedness or properness assumption. Dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A $T$-curve is strictly semistable if, locally on it and on $T$, it admits an etale morphism over the given affine base open [def-weil-etale-morphism] to $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$ or $\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv-a))$, where $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an open of $T$ and $a\in A$; polynomial rings use [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. For an integral scheme $Y$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], its function field is the local ring at its generic point. A birational quasi-modification $Y\to Z$ is a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] identifying the function field of $Y$ with the function field of the reduced irreducible component of $Z$ represented by $C$; equivalently, for a generic point $\eta_Y$ of $Y$ mapping to a generic point $\xi$ of $C$, the canonical residue-field map $\kappa_X(\xi)\to\kappa_Y(\eta_Y)$ induced by $Y\to Z$ is an isomorphism. A centred valuation of that component means a valuation subring $W\subset\kappa_X(\xi)$, together with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}W\to Z$ whose generic point is $\xi$. It lifts to $Y$ when this morphism factors through $Y$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, pp. 29--30; applied componentwise when the smooth generic fibre is disconnected; primary PDF read online, local archival copy WANTED (see report.md).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models] with empty marking: $X$ is reduced with finitely many components. Take a finite affine cover $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], each $A$ is finitely presented over $V$. Each component is horizontal. Indeed $V$-flatness makes multiplication by every nonzero $v\in V$ injective on $A$. If $v$ lay in a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$, choose, for every other minimal prime $\mathfrak q$, an element of $\mathfrak q\setminus\mathfrak p$ and multiply them. The resulting $b\notin\mathfrak p$ satisfies $vb=0$, since $A$ is reduced, a contradiction. Thus the function field $L$ of each component contains $K$ and is the function field of a smooth generic curve. It has transcendence degree one by [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg]. There are finitely many affine components to consider. A centred valuation whose closed centre is in $U$ factors through $U$: the inverse image of $U$ contains the closed point of the local spectrum and therefore all its generalizations.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, affine reduction; opening paragraph of section 4.2. Componentwise reduction written explicitly; affine finite presentation is Stacks 01TQ and transcendence degree is 0B1C.

proof.text: Fix one affine component with field $L$ and a centred valuation $W\subset L$. Put $R=W\cap K$. This is a valuation overring of $V$, and $R=V_{\mathfrak p}$ for $\mathfrak p=V\cap\mathfrak m_R$: every $s\in V\setminus\mathfrak p$ is invertible in $R$, while for $r\in R\setminus V$, the element $r^{-1}\in V$ is invertible in $R$, so belongs to $V\setminus\mathfrak p$. In particular $R$ has finite height. Localizing $\operatorname{Spec}W\to U$ by nonzero elements of $V$ gives a centre on $U_\eta$. This localization is $KW$ as in [lem-trf-valued-curve-etale-parameter]; inverting $V\setminus\{0\}$ or $R\setminus\{0\}$ gives the same subring of $L$, since both yield all of $K$. The morphism lands in the component of the smooth generic curve with field $L$. Apply that parameter theorem to obtain $t\in W$, $F=K(t)$ and $O=W\cap F$ such that $O\to W$ is etale and $L/F$ is finite. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}O$ has its prescribed centre on $P=\operatorname{Spec}V[t]$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, parameter paragraph; Theorem 2.1.8 and Lemma 2.1.6. The localization description of valuation overrings is the first paragraph on printed p. 7.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-birational-riemann-zariski-neighbourhoods](iii) for $P$ and $O$: write $O=\varinjlim A_j$, where $D_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ is an affine neighbourhood of the centre on an integral proper birational model $P_j\to P$, with $A_j\subset O\subset F$ and $\operatorname{Frac}A_j=F$. The index category is small and filtered on rings, as required in the subsequent descent statements. The morphism $P_j\to P$ is a reduced modification: a finite set of algebra generators on affine charts gives a dense isomorphism open after clearing their denominators in $F$. By [lem-trf-valuation-horizontal-curve-models], $P_j$ is a $T$-curve and its generic fibre is $P_\eta$. Consequently $(D_j)_\eta$ is an open of the affine line, and $A_j$ is finitely presented over $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. Here $P$ itself is the affine-line strictly semistable model, with smooth generic fibre and empty marking.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, limit over modifications of the rational curve; Lemma 3.2.2 and section 4.2. Finite-presentation version of its approximation argument.

proof.text: Since $O\to W$ is etale, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-filtered-colimit-descent] gives an etale $A_j$-algebra $B_j$ and an identification $O\otimes_{A_j}B_j=W$. For each later index replace $B_j$ by its base change; these remain etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and their filtered colimit is $W$. For every such index, $B_j\otimes_{A_j}F=W\otimes_OF=L$. To check the last equality, the left localization is a domain algebraic over the field $F$, and every nonzero algebraic element has its inverse in the same algebra by its minimal polynomial; its fraction field is $L$. Moreover $B_j$ is $A_j$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Tensor the injection $A_j\hookrightarrow F$ with $B_j$ to see that $B_j\hookrightarrow L$. Thus $B_j$ is a domain. Its fraction field is exactly $L$, since its localization by the nonzero elements of $A_j$ already equals $L$. This also verifies that no unwanted generic factor has been introduced by descent.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, approximation paragraph; agent refinement using Stacks 00U2(9), (3), (6). Descending the etale valuation algebra directly makes the intermediate flattening unnecessary.

proof.text: The given centre determines a $V$-algebra map $A\to W$. Since $A$ is finitely presented over $V$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] to $W=\varinjlim B_j$. After increasing $j$ this map factors through $A\to B_j\to W$. Under the inclusions into $L$ from Step 4 its generic map is the original component map $A\to L$. In particular the kernel is precisely the prime defining that component of $U$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, descent from the valuation local ring; Stacks 00QO (lemma-characterize-finite-presentation), (1) implies (3). Agent finite-presentation implementation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-strict-semistable-cofinality] to the modification $P_j\to P$. It supplies an integral strictly semistable model $Z\to P$ dominating $P_j$, with the same generic fibre. Integrality follows as well from the dense integral isomorphism open in a modification: schematic density kills any sections vanishing there, so every nonempty affine chart embeds into its function field. By [lem-trf-birational-riemann-zariski-neighbourhoods], $O$ has a unique lift to $Z$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $E=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of its centre contained in the inverse image of $D_j$. The whole morphism $\operatorname{Spec}O\to Z$ factors through $E$, since its closed point does. We have $A_j\subset C\subset O$, $\operatorname{Frac}C=F$, and $E_\eta$ is an open of the affine line. Also $C$ is finitely presented over $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation].

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, final paragraph: enlarge the rational-curve modification using Proposition 4.3.1, then restrict about the valuation centre.

proof.text: Set $B=B_j\otimes_{A_j}C$ and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The map $Y\to E$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The maps $B_j\to W$ and $C\to O\to W$ agree on $A_j$, so give $B\to W$ and a factorization of the original centre through $Y$. Since $B$ is $C$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], tensoring $C\hookrightarrow F$ embeds $B$ into $B\otimes_CF=L$. Hence $B$ is a domain with fraction field $L$. The ring $C$ is $V$-flat because $E$ is an open of the $T$-curve $Z$, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Flatness of $V\to B$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp]. The etale map $C\to B$ is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], as is $V\to C$; their composite is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. Thus $Y\to T$ is flat and finitely presented, with a genuine valuation lift.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, etale model over the strictly semistable rational model; Stacks 02GO, 00U2(6), 00HC, 00F4(2).

proof.text: The integral finite-type $K$-scheme $Y_\eta$ has field $L$, so [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] gives $\dim Y_\eta=1$. For any prime $\mathfrak p\subset V$, apply [lem-trf-valuation-domain-fibre-dimensions] to the finite-type domain $B\otimes_VV_{\mathfrak p}$ over the valuation ring $V_{\mathfrak p}$. Its generic fibre is $B\otimes_VK$ and has dimension one. Every nonempty fibre over $\mathfrak p$ is therefore equidimensional of dimension one; the same holds at the generic point by the preceding dimension computation. This proves the required pure relative dimension. Finally $Y_\eta\to E_\eta$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; its source is smooth of relative dimension one over $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] and [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], since $E_\eta$ is an open of the smooth affine line.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, final etale locus; curve conditions made explicit using Stacks 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres) and 0B1C.

proof.text: Restrict the strictly semistable charts of $Z$ to $E$. Compose these with $Y\to E$; the composites are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Thus $Y$ has exactly the affine-line or $uv-a$ charts in the stated definition of strict semistability, so is strictly semistable. The map $A\to B$ from Steps 5 and 7 defines an affine morphism $Y\to U$. It is of finite type: a finite set of $V$-algebra generators of $B$ also generates it as an $A$-algebra. Since $U$ is a quasi-compact open of the quasi-separated $X$, the composition $Y\to U\to X$ is separated and of finite type. It identifies its function field with the chosen component field $L$ and lifts $W$, as required for a birational quasi-modification.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, last sentence; strict semistability from composition of etale charts, Stacks 02GN.

proof.text: For completeness verify the whole generic map is an open immersion. Its image is in the component $H$ of $U_\eta$ with function field $L$; the components of a smooth curve are disjoint and open, since their local rings are normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal], hence domains, and there are finitely many components. The morphism $Y_\eta\to H$ is affine, finite type and birational. Both source and target are integral one-dimensional finite-type $K$-schemes. The generic fibre is a single point. Over a closed point of $H$, a nonzero element of its prime ideal stays nonzero in the domain of $Y_\eta$, so every prime in that fibre is nonzero and hence maximal. The fibre has dimension zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-quasifinite-zero-fibre-dimension] this is an everywhere quasi-finite morphism. The affine target $H$ is qcqs, so [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] gives a quasi-compact open immersion $Y_\eta\hookrightarrow M$ with $M\to H$ finite.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.3, generic-open refinement requested by the item; Stacks 0397 (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0), 05K0 (lemma-quasi-finite-separated-pass-through-finite).

proof.text: Let $N$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $Y_\eta\hookrightarrow M$, using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel]. On an affine of $M$ meeting $Y_\eta$, its coordinate ring modulo the kernel embeds into the function field $L$, so is a domain; these affine images have the same generic point. Hence $N$ is integral, finite over $H$, and has function field $L$. Its intersection with the open $Y_\eta$ is all of $Y_\eta$ with its original structure, because the kernel ideal restricts to zero there. Thus $Y_\eta\to N$ is an open immersion. The target $H$ is normal by [lem-sc-smooth-normal]. Apply [lem-trf-finite-birational-normal-iso] to $N\to H$: it is an isomorphism. Therefore $Y_\eta\to H\hookrightarrow X_\eta$ is an open immersion, proving the additional generic clause rather than merely birationality.

source.place: Generic-open refinement of Proposition 4.3.3; Stacks 0AB1 (lemma-finite-birational-over-normal), with the schematic-image kernel description.

proof.text: For each affine component $U_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p_\alpha)$, Steps 2--11 construct a suitable $Y\to U_\alpha$ around each of its centred valuations. The factorization through $U_\alpha$ is scheme-theoretic: $A\to B\hookrightarrow L$ has kernel $\mathfrak p_\alpha$. Apply [lem-trf-birational-riemann-zariski-neighbourhoods](ii): the valuations which lift to this $Y$ form an open subspace of $\operatorname{Val}_L(U_\alpha)$. These opens cover that space by construction, and clause (i) makes it quasi-compact. Choose finitely many such $Y$ for each affine component, and take their union as a finite list over the finite affine cover of $X$. Every centred valuation factors through an affine containing its closed centre and through its component, so lifts to one entry of the list. Each entry is integral, strictly semistable, and has the generic-open property from Step 11. If $X$ is empty, the empty list works. This proves all clauses without changing $T$ or its fraction field.

previous.old_statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $X$ be a $T$-curve with smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. There are finitely many integral strictly semistable $T$-curves $Y_i$ and birational quasi-modifications $Y_i\to X$ such that every centred valuation of every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$ lifts to some $Y_i$. Each generic map $(Y_i)_\eta\to X_\eta$ identifies $(Y_i)_\eta$ with an open subscheme. A $T$-curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one, without a separatedness or properness assumption. Dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A $T$-curve is strictly semistable if, locally on it and on $T$, it admits an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism] to $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$ or $\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv-a))$, where $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an open of $T$ and $a\in A$; polynomial rings use [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. For an integral scheme $Y$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], its function field is the local ring at its generic point. A birational quasi-modification $Y\to Z$ is a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] identifying the function field of $Y$ with that of one irreducible component of the reduced scheme $Z$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. A centred valuation of that component means a valuation subring $W$ of its function field, together with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}W\to Z$ inducing the generic-point map. It lifts to $Y$ when this morphism factors through $Y$.
previous.what: The base Lean statement had two defects. Second, its valuation clause quantified an unrelated field L and used unreduced stalks. The corrected statement uses the canonical component field `X.residueField ξ`, requires `z.base (⊥ : PrimeSpectrum W) = ξ`, and requires `(y i).base ηᵢ = ξ ∧ Function.Bijective ((y i).residueFieldMap ηᵢ).hom`, the canonical generic-point residue-field map.
